findings.title: Public names removed from `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed` with no importers updated
findings.body: This PR deletes the module-level names `mark_failed_threshold`, `create_issue_platform_occurrence`, `get_failure_reason`, `get_monitor_environment_context` and the `SimpleCheckIn` TypedDict from `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed` and re-homes them (under new names in some cases) in `sentry/monitors/logic/incidents.py`, `sentry/monitors/logic/incident_occurrence.py` and `sentry/monitors/types.py`. No other file in the PR is updated. Any production module or test that imports these symbols from `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed`, or that monkeypatches them by path (e.g. `mock.patch("sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed.create_issue_platform_occurrence")`), will now raise ImportError/AttributeError, or worse, silently patch nothing and let real Kafka occurrences be produced in tests. The reorganization should be accompanied by updates to all call sites/patch targets (grep for the old names) before merging.

findings.title: `get_monitor_environment_context` returns the raw config, discarding the humanized `schedule_type`
findings.body: The function copies `monitor.config` into `config` and replaces the numeric `schedule_type` with its display value, but the returned dict sets `"config": monitor_environment.monitor.config` — the original object, not `config`. The computed copy is dead code, so the monitor context attached to the issue occurrence event contains the raw integer `schedule_type` instead of the human readable one (e.g. `0` rather than `crontab`). Since this code is being moved into a new module anyway, it is a good time to return `config` instead.

findings.title: `get_failure_reason` produces a malformed string when no statuses are recognized
findings.body: `status_counts` only counts statuses present in `HUMAN_FAILURE_STATUS_MAP` (error/missed/timeout). If `failed_checkins` is empty or contains only other statuses (e.g. `IN_PROGRESS`/`OK`), the counter is empty, the `sum(...) == 1` branch is skipped, `get_text_list([])` returns an empty string and the function returns the nonsensical " check-ins detected", which is then shown to users as the issue's "Failure reason" evidence. A fallback such as the generic "A failed check-in was detected" message mentioned in the docstring should be returned for the empty case.

findings.title: Docstring of `get_failure_reason` is misspelled and documents output the function cannot produce
findings.body: The docstring reads "Builds a humam readible string" (should be "human readable") and lists example outputs that do not match the implementation: "2 missed check-ins, 1 timeout check-in and 1 error check-in were detected" (the code emits "2 missed, 1 timeout and 1 error check-ins detected") and "A failed check-in was detected", which is never returned by any branch. Since the code is being moved into a new module, the docstring should be corrected so it doesn't mislead future readers about the generated user-facing text.
